instruction: Refine a 105-question what-to-think experiment plan, including shared chunks, prompt goals, current model candidates and request-time token metrics.
scope: Unpaced causal-prefix content study before inference implementation
sub_questions: How should small speech units be grouped into useful private-work blocks?
Which private goals preserve people, facts, updates and supported consequences?
How should native thinking and earlier private output be counted?
Which reproducible local text/audio models and speaker-transcription pipelines fit the study?

themes: Earlier private results must be treated as fallible, source-linked context.
Model-specific native thinking visibility and template behavior require verification.
Stable chunking and frozen prompt selection are necessary to isolate content choices.
gaps: No cited paper validates the proposed 20–45 second thresholds on this question bank; tune them on disjoint development data.
No selected model has a new all-105 result in this planning task.
Lower request-time thinking alone does not imply lower total cost or real-time feasibility.
search_method: Multiple independent queries on incremental reasoning, chunking, memory goals, current text/audio releases and diarization; primary papers/model cards checked directly.
